candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 21:4-9. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Jn 3:14 (verbatim Christological appropriation).
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the bronze serpent lifted on the standard for the healing of the bitten (Num 21:8-9), Ephrem reads the lifted-up-serpent as the canonical Old-Testament prefigurement of the Crucifixion — taken up verbatim by Christ himself in Jn 3:14: 'as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up.' The bronze that looks like serpent but contains no venom prefigures Christ-in-the-likeness-of-sinful-flesh-but-without-sin (Rom 8:3). Looking-and-living is the canonical pattern of faith. Tewahedo Mäsqäl theology cites Num 21:8 alongside Jn 3:14 as the canonical doubled-anchor of the Cross-as-healing-standard for the bitten world.
